subject: Physics
title: Electric Charge: Like Charges Repel, Unlike Attract
summary: Those sparks when you pull off a sweater come from electric charge. How rubbing moves electrons, what positive and negative mean, and why like charges repel.

notes.title: 01 – Electric Charge: Like Charges Repel, Unlike Attract

keyPoints: Rubbing two bodies **transfers electrons** from one to the other.
Charge is **not created**: the pair's total stays the same.
The body that **loses electrons** becomes positive; the one that **gains** them becomes negative.
Glass rubbed with silk is **positive**, and the silk **negative**. Plastic rubbed with fur is **negative**.

quiz.q: When glass is rubbed with silk, the glass becomes:
quiz.explain: It loses electrons to the silk.
Only electrons move; the total stays the same.

simulation.reason: Rubbing a pair yourself and watching the total stay 0, then choosing any two rubbed objects to predict attraction or repulsion, tests the rule on cases the video does not show.
simulation.objective: See that rubbing only moves electrons, then predict which rubbed objects repel or attract.
instructions: Choose a pair and press Rub once.
Watch the two charges: the pair's total stays 0.
Pick two objects and predict: will they repel or attract?
